items.problem: Bootstrap inventory omitted linked/shared project inputs and emitted an empty-defer marker inconsistent with its validator.
items.evidence: lessons.json dev_agent_struggles[0]; skill-defects.json items[0] and [3]; session-log.txt bootstrap copied 4 files and validator later emitted a false defer warning.
items.root_cause: Directory traversal was used as a proxy for the project source graph, and bootstrap/validator empty-state contracts diverged.
items.change: Parse old-style csproj Compile/ApplicationDefinition/Page/Content/None/PRIResource/AppxManifest items, expand common properties including GetDirectoryNameOfFileAbove, honor Link target paths, report linked counts, and emit the validator's exact no-defer sentence.
items.expected_effect: Shared shell, scenario XAML, styles, and assets enter the normal mapping/triage pipeline automatically, eliminating manual reconstruction and false defer warnings.
items.falsifiable_check: On the same PowerGrid source, bootstrap copies 20 mapped files with linkedFileCount=16; App.xaml, MainPage.xaml, both scenario XAML files, Styles/Styles.xaml, and shared assets exist without manual additions, and zero-defer validation emits PASS rather than WARN.

items.problem: Standalone launch validation rejected valid builds produced without an explicit Platform property.
items.evidence: skill-defects.json item[1]; session-log.txt Test-AppLaunch returned unavailable immediately before validator rebuilt and smoke-launched successfully.
items.root_cause: The launcher hard-coded bin/<arch>/Debug instead of identifying complete output layouts.
items.change: Recursively find the newest directory under bin containing both an executable and AppxManifest, normalizing AppX subfolders.
items.expected_effect: The same launcher works for bin/Debug and bin/<Platform>/Debug layouts and no longer sends agents into redundant foreground runs.
items.falsifiable_check: After plain dotnet build and after dotnet build -p:Platform=x64, Test-AppLaunch -Target resolves a complete layout instead of returning 'No build output found'.

items.problem: Build-diagnostic guidance misidentified secondary WMC9999 failures and omitted a common DispatcherQueue collision.
items.evidence: skill-defects.json item[2] and skill-coverage-gaps.json item[0]; the run spent multiple turns inspecting generated XAML and hit CS0104 for the two DispatcherQueue types.
items.root_cause: The prose overfit one WMC9999 cause and showed unqualified threading examples without the Windows.System collision caveat.
items.change: State that earlier CS/specific WMC diagnostics take precedence over WMC9999, and add explicit Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueue qualification guidance.
items.expected_effect: Agents fix the primary diagnostic first and resolve the common type collision directly instead of inspecting generated output or chasing resource keys.
items.falsifiable_check: On a rerun with the same diagnostics, DispatcherQueue is qualified before build and WMC9999 investigation begins with preceding CS/WMC errors; the generated-file inspection detour is absent.
items.tier_3_justification: Neither transformation is safe to automate mechanically: import usage and the primary cause of an internal XAML compiler failure require local semantic context. A template would encode the same fallible assumption, so focused diagnostic instructions are the highest feasible tier.

deferred_to_human: Tier 0/evaluation: investigate why the launchable UWP reference remains on the platform sample splash screen. Do not address this by changing migration or evaluation skills in this improvement.
